result.keywords: This article examines a fictional tradition of coastal confectionery, focusing on ceremonial sugar sculptures, seasonal spice infusions, and communal tasting rituals in a small island society. It analyzes ingredient symbolism, preparation methods, and the role of artisan bakeries in preserving oral history. The study contrasts domestic dessert practices with market-day exchange customs and includes a descriptive case study of moon-pressed citrus syrup, braided almond wafers, and salt-glazed serving vessels.
result.title: Moonlit Lanterns in a Basin of Salt
